title: Independent artist admin & payments
short: Receive sats, get booked, store contracts. No label, no manager, no US bank.
what: Indie Caribbean artists are paid microscopic per-stream royalties by global DSPs, can't afford a manager or label, and have no good tool for tour planning, door-sales splits, merch, contracts, IP/publishing rights, gig booking.
how: An app on Voyager lets an artist receive payment in sats, or local fiat via a Mostro ramp, get booked by venues, and store contracts — all without giving up their identity or paying 0.003¢ per stream.

title: Caribbean-to-Caribbean commerce
short: A buyer-seller app that works across the region without a 30% cut.
what: A Barbadian wants to buy something from Grenada and has no idea who to trust 30 minutes away. There is no Caribbean hub marketplace.
how: A buyer-seller app on Voyager, using the v3 protocol's listing + order events, gives discoverability, payment, and dispute arbitration across the region without an intermediary that takes a 30% cut or a payment processor that won't serve them.

title: Concierge & tourism
short: High-touch trip planning where the operator keeps the booking minus a tiny routing fee.
what: High-touch trip planning for visitors to Barbados (and eventually other islands). The operator is the brand, the planner is the tool.
how: The operator gets paid in sats or local fiat. The customer pays with whatever they have: Lightning, Lightning-via-ramp, or USD via Mostro. The operator keeps 100% of the booking minus a tiny Lightning routing fee. Trip Planner is the working reference for this use case.

title: Creator monetization without US bank
short: Receive Lightning, optionally convert to local fiat via Mostro. No DSP needed.
what: Caribbean creators get monetized on YouTube/Reels/TikTok only if they have a US bank. Most don't, and the cut is brutal.
how: An app on Voyager lets a creator receive sats directly via Lightning, optionally convert to local fiat (JMD, TTD, BBD, XCD, GYD, HTG, BSD) via Mostro, and access a payment channel that doesn't require a US bank account.

title: Island-hopping logistics
short: Regional transport booking and payment on the same primitives as everything else.
what: Cheaper to fly Barbados → LA than Barbados → Trinidad. No ferry system. Inter-island logistics is a known gap.
how: Apps on Voyager might integrate regional transport booking and payment. The protocol doesn't need to know about boats, but the toolkit's payment and identity primitives make a transport app 10x easier to ship than starting from a hosted payments stack.

title: Cultural discovery & hub
short: A Caribbean-keyed social surface with identity built in. No platform to lose.
what: There is no place online where Caribbean people just hang out and don't have to explain themselves. This is not a payment problem. It's an identity + discovery problem.
how: Voyager's Nostr-keypair login and relay-set gives any builder a turnkey way to make a Caribbean-keyed community surface (timeline, group chat, marketplace) without rebuilding identity.

title: Venue & performer matchmaking
short: Verifiable reputation, signed gig records, atomic settlement between both sides.
what: Indie artists can't find venues; venues can't find reliable indie artists. The less the artist knows, the easier it is to take advantage.
how: An app on Voyager can store verifiable reputation (zaps, past-gigs as Nostr events), let venues post open slots, let artists apply, and settle payments atomically — without a CAA-style gatekeeper.

title: Sports, carnival, diaspora coordination
short: Group bookings, tickets, remittances on the same primitives as everything else.
what: West Indies cricket plays as one team; carnivals happen across NYC, London, Toronto. Diaspora coordination is the unspoken use case.
how: Apps on Voyager can coordinate group bookings, ticket sales, and remittances for the diaspora community with the same primitives — no need to integrate 5 payment processors.
